messages:
sasha: Heads-up — a customer hit duplicate billing when their client reconnected during a canary swap. They resumed the SSE stream and we ended up charging tokens twice because the resume went to a different route instance. Anyone seen this pattern?
jon: Can you paste the request/headers and the console trace?
sasha: Minimal repro from logs: client got 408, retried with resume token, stream resumed on route=v2 instead of route=v1 and both attempts show billed tokens in the console. infra-bot flagged a billing spike: alert id 98312.
jon: Hmm. If resume is just a client-supplied token that server redeems, we need to ensure the redemption is idempotent across routes. Right now we check local cache per-instance.
maya: Idea: make resume token a signed blob that includes session_id + route_id + expiry. Server accepts it only if signature valid and route_id matches, or if signature shows it's unredeemed. But binding to route_id will break resume when we move routes during rollouts.
ryan: Binding to route_id is safer for quotas. If we allow cross-route redemption, someone could replay a token against a cheaper route and bypass limits. Also a signed blob is extra crypto overhead on hot path.
lina: Alternative: keep resume negotiation server-side. Client sends only a short resume_key. We maintain central resume state (redis) keyed by global session id. On reconnect we check resume_key->last_ack and decide whether to bill. But that adds a cross-region coordination hit.
sasha: To inform product/console teams, we need better telemetry. Proposal: add these fields to stream events: reconnect_reason (network/408/idle), resume_token_hash, original_route_id, resumed_on_route_id, resume_accepted(boolean), resume_billed(boolean). Console can then show per-route resume counts and cases where route drift caused double-billing.
maya: I can add runtime labels for reconnect_reason and resumed_on_route_id in the logs. We'll need a small schema change for events. Suggest adding a new enum 'resume_result' with values: accepted_no_bill, accepted_billed, rejected_stale, rejected_auth.
ryan: Also debating exact server behavior: Option A) Accept resume only if session_id matches and mark token consumed atomically in a central store (no cross-route double-bill). Option B) Accept resume locally with a short-lived distributed lease and have reconciler fix dup bills later (eventual fix but cheaper). Which do we want?
jon: From UX/ops perspective A is best: no customer-visible duplication. But A increases latency and state complexity. B is risky for billing accuracy and will cause support noise.
sasha: For rollout plan: we can implement A as opt-in behind a feature-flag for a few customers (dedicated & enterprise) while we measure impact. Console rollout page should indicate which tenants are on the centralized-resume path.
ryan: Small API proposal: add header X-Resume-Token: <signed> and X-Resume-Mode: centralized|local; but that exposes internal routing. Maybe prefer a query param ?resume=1 when the client requests resume semantics for a session created after rollout. Backwards compatible default = local.
Maya: Example header sketch:```
GET /v1/stream?sse=true
Authorization: Bearer tok_xxx
X-Resume-Token: eyJhbGci...
X-Client-Session: sess-012345
```
We should never accept X-Resume-Token from unauthenticated clients.
infra-bot: alert: billing-dup-spike 2026-03-18T21:12Z (count=42)
jon: We also need console UX: a new tile on rollout page showing "resume_accept_rate" and "resume_billed_rate" by route shard + a trace link to the stream events. That will help SRE quickly identify cross-route resumes.
lina: I'll mock a small UI change — left column shows rollout percentage, right column shows resume drift heatmap.
sasha: Plan agreed-ish: maya implements telemetry labels + event schema; ryan prototypes central resume store (opt-in); jon wires console panels to new metrics; lina builds the rollout UI mock. We'll do a short spike to measure redis ops.
deploy-bot: sasha pushed 2 commits to main (PR #4287) — "stream: add resume labels to runtime events"
ryan: One more: we must decide billing accounting if reconciliation runs later and detects duplicate charge — automatic refund or manual? Product to decide.
sasha: Filed a short RFC with options, tagging @product billing. We'll review tomorrow 10am. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
